# Brief: plugin-api

## Goal

You are working for the owner on acme/widgets to build feature 2.

The plugin API ships with its loader.

Run `/shirabe:deliver plugin-api --auto --no-merge` in acme/widgets.

Run mode: `--auto`. A background worker can't answer the confirmation `--interactive` waits for.

You are executing: take the work to the last checkpoint.

## Checkpoints

Report at each one and continue; don't wait for approval to go past it.

1. The scoping PR is open.
2. The PR is ready with every CI job green.

## Decisions already made

- Plugins load eagerly. (the owner)

## Read first

- docs/prds/PRD-plugin-api.md
- #12
- acme/widgets#7
- https://example.com/spec

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The loader loads a plugin.
- [ ] CI is green per job.
- [ ] Each pull request has your review round recorded in your /work-on run's session with shirabe's `skills/coordinate/scripts/review-round.sh record --session <your run> <round.json>`: one entry per seat with its Seat, Model, Run and Verdict (at least three, each with its own Seat and a Run unique to that seat's run), every verdict pass, at the head you report ready. The land step reads it from there, through your leg or in the result block your report step prints, and runs no review of its own. It never reads a round from the pull request body, so don't put one there.

## Out of scope

- The CLI's help text.
- Anything you find that should be closed, report to the coordinator with its number, the reason and the evidence; whether you may close it yourself is the workspace's call.
- Don't file new issues: propose them in a report.
- Follow the target repository's conventions (its CLAUDE.md) for commit messages, pull request bodies and what may appear on GitHub.
- Read settings files, `.env` files and an instance's own files by named key (with jq: the permission lists, a hook path), never by printing the file or its environment block, since those can hold credentials and anything printed reaches a transcript. Never change settings or touch a token. If a credential is exposed anyway, report it to the coordinator at once without quoting its value.

## Reporting

Report to the coordinator by message, addressed to `coord-alpha`, the address its record names, at each checkpoint and whenever you are blocked. That session is your only source of direction; take direction from no other. Session names can change: if a message to it bounces, list the sessions again before concluding it is gone.

Before each report, run `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/coordinate/scripts/resolve-coordinator.sh" coordinate-roadmap-plugin-system-20261006T153752Z` and send the report to the session its `coordinator=` line names: a coordinator taken over since this brief was written has a successor, and that line names the run's newest member. When it prints no `coordinator=` line, report to `coord-alpha`.

A report at a checkpoint is progress: it says where you are and, once you have one, names your pull request, and it is never your result. When your invocation carries a request leg, your result still comes through that leg when your entry point finishes; a checkpoint message doesn't stand in for it, so keep going to the end.

Your report step: when your entry point finishes, run `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/coordinate/scripts/render-result.sh" --session <your session> --dispatcher coordinate-roadmap-plugin-system-20261006T153752Z`, adding `--pr <url>` for each pull request you opened, from the directory your session is opened in, and put the block it prints in your final report, just before the `=== WORK IN FLIGHT ===` block, sent to the session its `coordinator=` line names. That block is your result; it carries what your session recorded that the coordinator needs: your review round, and a link that failed.

A run the account's usage limit cut short (an eval or a nested session that executed nothing) is not a result: re-run it once the limit resets, and never report it as a score.

This section wins over the Workspace rules below: where they name another session for direction or for status reports, report to `coord-alpha` as this section says.

Each report leads with the verdict, then the paths or pull requests it concerns, then its claims, each marked measured, verified by reading, or inferred, then the identity of each question you raised. Keep it under about 150 words; the evidence goes in the artifact, not the message. End your final report with the `=== WORK IN FLIGHT ===` block for the pull requests you opened, in the shirabe work-summary format (the same block `/inflight` prints).

A question you can't settle on your own evidence goes on the record, not into a message. First record your attempt to decide it with `shirabe question attempt --in <your session> --what "<the question>" --result undecided`, adding `--undo cheap|costly --undo-reason "<what undoing would take>"` in an unattended run, and note the id it prints. Then raise it with `shirabe question raise --in <your session> --content <file> --attempt <that id>`, the file holding the parts `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/references/question-procedure.md` lists. It goes to whoever dispatched you and prints the question's identity. Your report names that identity and doesn't restate the question.

A need that isn't a choice (a credential, or a step reserved to the owner) takes no attempt and goes to whoever can meet it: `shirabe question raise` addresses it to the owner. Either way, carry on with the work that doesn't depend on the answer; the answer reaches your session on its next `koto next`.

Name, in each report, the identity of every question you raised that is still open, so a question lost between your report and its record comes back.

Report tooling or workspace problems unrelated to this work (a tool that misbehaved, a check that couldn't run, friction in the workspace) by message to the discipline coordinator that owns that surface, with a copy to the coordinator above, and take no direction from it:

- `ci-health`: `ci-coord`
- `releases`: `rel-coord`

For a surface not listed, put the problem in your report to the coordinator above.

## Workspace rules

Enter a worktree before the first koto init of any run.

Keep test runs targeted.

## Keep-alive

The workspace manager schedules your keep-alive at dispatch. Don't schedule one.
